# Human Agency Protocol (HAP)

> HAP is an open, MIT-licensed protocol for bounded AI-agent authority. Humans
> hold authority. Agents borrow it, bounded, and every consequential act carries
> proof the loan was honoured before it happened.

The central invariant is **no mandate, no ticket; no ticket, no execution**. A
person gives an agent a **mandate** — bounds, scope, duration, commitment mode.
Each consequential action obtains a signed **mandate ticket** *before* it runs;
if the ticket cannot be issued — outside the mandate, over a limit, approval
missing, revoked, expired, Authority Server unreachable — the action does not
happen. The ticket is a precondition, not a record; afterwards the same ticket
is the evidence, and it puts an identifiable person behind that one act.

HAP defines three roles:

- **Authority Server** — holds the signing key. Signs the mandate. Enforces
  cumulative limits, approval and revocation. **Issues and signs** the ticket
  (Ed25519). Can refuse.
- **Gatekeeper** — holds the bounds and scope locally. Verifies the mandate,
  checks the attempted action, then **requests** a ticket pre-flight,
  fail-closed. Keeps the complete signed ticket as the person's own evidence.
  The Gatekeeper never issues a ticket; it asks.
- **Executor** — holds the credentials. Runs the downstream tool, only after a
  valid ticket exists.

Vocabulary (one word per thing on the wire, in the specification, and in
public): mandate (never "attestation" or "grant"), mandate ticket / ticket
(never "receipt"), bounds (the enforced limits), scope (the local signed
dimension; never "context"), Mandate Owner (the identifiable person; never
"Decision Owner"), without a mandate (the condition the protocol exists to end).
Access is not a mandate.

HAP is not a permission system, not a control model (control governs the agent;
a mandate governs the delegation), not a guarantee of compliance (it is enabling
infrastructure for regimes such as EU AI Act Art. 14 and ISO 42001), and not
agent sandboxing.

## Specification

- [Core Specification](https://humanagencyprotocol.org/protocol): the normative protocol — profiles, bounds, scope, gates, mandates, mandate tickets, content binding, read authorization, owner signatures, and the behaviour required of each role.
- [Governance](https://humanagencyprotocol.org/governance): how HAP is governed — invariant constraints instead of institutions. No central authority, no registry, no approval process.
- [Conformance Vectors](https://humanagencyprotocol.org/vectors): the published answer key — canonical strings and hashes, payload signatures under published test keys, the profile hash, and the refusals an implementation must produce. Raw files at /vectors/*.json.
- [Changelog](https://humanagencyprotocol.org/changelog): non-normative record of what each version promoted into the binding surface, under which rule, and what was retired.
- [Review and Future Directions](https://humanagencyprotocol.org/review): non-normative forward ledger — open directions with their targets and the deviation rules that bind every implementation. Implementation status is not part of the specification.
- [Provenance](https://humanagencyprotocol.org/provenance): the dated record of every published version and the first public appearance of each concept.

## Full text

- [Complete specification as plain text](https://humanagencyprotocol.org/context.txt): every specification document concatenated into a single file, intended for pasting into an AI assistant.

## Implementations

- [Suveren](https://www.suveren.ai): a commercial HAP-compliant implementation. The Suveren Gateway (open source) implements the Gatekeeper and Executor roles; the Suveren Authority Server implements the Authority Server role, hosted or self-hosted. Its implementation report against the specification: https://github.com/humanagencyprotocol/hap-e2e/blob/main/CONFORMANCE.md
- [hap-core on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@humanagencyp/hap-core): the open-source protocol library — verification, canonicalisation and hashing, mandate decode/verify, content binding, identity.
- [GitHub](https://github.com/humanagencyprotocol/hap-protocol): specification source, conformance vectors, and provenance record.
